subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What Telegram reliability contract should OpenClaw use when a voice update's Telegram `message.date` is much older than dispatch time and the resulting direct-message turn aborts without a visible reply?
rationale: The code can expose the missing timestamp comparison and fallback gap, but the restart threshold, alert/retry behavior, and user-facing failure text are product and reliability choices that can change live Telegram behavior.

options.title: Define the combined watchdog and fallback contract
options.body: Set a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart rule, and direct-message fallback behavior, then implement and prove it across polling, spool drain, and dispatch tests.

options.title: Split the work across adjacent items
options.body: Review the open polling PR for sleep-gap behavior separately and keep the no-response recovery work under the open voice transcript recovery issue.

options.title: Wait for a fresh live reproduction
options.body: Defer code changes until a current-main Telegram voice trace proves the exact delayed-dispatch and abort path, accepting that the issue remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Define the combined watchdog and fallback contract
recommendation.body: Set a source-age threshold, diagnostic/restart rule, and direct-message fallback behavior, then implement and prove it across polling, spool drain, and dispatch tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Telegram liveness, spool, and retry work is closest to the source-age and drain-side decision surface.
